correctness.rationale: The upper bound follows by applying the published componentwise generalized-derivation submajorization estimate and iterating its finite-direct-sum stability. The lower bound combines the published atomic type-I-infinity lower-estimate construction componentwise; distribution functions add over finite central sums, so dilation commutes with the merged rearrangement and the resulting norm loss tends to one. The one-factor, positive, and explicit two-factor Schatten tests are consistent.

originality.rationale: To the best of our knowledge, the recent primary source gives the exact self-adjoint formula on factors and the exact non-factor formula for positive implementers, but not the finite-center center-local formula. Targeted searches found no equivalent finite-atomic-center statement or the explicit cross-center sharpness mechanism. The principal residual risk is the uninspected full text of the older Fialkow and Fialkow--Loebl norm-ideal papers.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the correct exact replacement for the factor formula on finite atomic centers and exhibits a strict two-summand obstruction to naive global sign matching. It applies uniformly to arbitrary symmetrically normed sequence ideals.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
